title: Why Do Cat Eyes Glow? Roads Copied Them!

phrases: Why do a cat's eyes glow in the dark?
And why do roads have glowing eyes too?
Here's the twist: neither one makes its own light!
Watch this. Light zooms into the cat's eye.
It goes through the lens, like a magnifying glass.
At the back is a shiny layer, like a tiny mirror.
The light bounces off it, and comes back out!
So the eye gets two chances to catch the light.
That's how cats see when it's super dark.
No flashlight needed. Sorry, flashlight!
And that bounce is the glow you see!
But wait... what about the road?
In England, a man named Percy Shaw
drove home on dark, foggy roads.
One famous story says a cat's shining eyes
showed him the edge of the road.
He told a few stories, but cats got the fame!
In 1934, he patented road studs called catseyes.
Each stud has glass in front, like the cat's lens,
and a mirror behind, like the shiny layer.
Car lights hit it and bounce straight back to the driver.
No batteries. No wires. Just bouncing light!
When a tyre presses it, rubber wipes the glass,
like an eyelid blinking! Clean again!
Cat eyes and road eyes. Same smart trick!
Where have you seen glowing road eyes?
